deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated layers. One is an expository draft in German, §4a 'Intervalle', belonging to the theory of cuts (Schnitte). The other is a set of scratch computations in a quadratic field.

A. Intervals (left column, German text).
- The two classes A1, A2 of a cut are said to be special cases of a more general notion. A system A of rational numbers is called an Intervall if every number lying between two numbers of A also belongs to A. In modern terms, A is an order-convex subset of Q.
- Examples: Q itself (R in Dedekind's notation) is an interval. Each class of a cut is an interval: if a1 is in A1, every smaller number is in A1; if a2 is in A2, every larger number is in A2.
- Converse: suppose A1 is closed downward and there exist numbers not in A1. Then every number not in A1 exceeds every number in A1, so (A1, Q\A1) is a cut. Dually, an upward-closed proper subset is a second class.
- The next page continues with Stueck (sub-interval), benachbart (disjoint intervals whose union is an interval), and the complements A', A'' that complete A to R.

B. Quadratic-field computations (right column and top).
- Let theta be a root of t^2 - b t + c = 0, so theta^2 = b theta - c. Elements are x + y theta with x, y rational, also written as pairs (x, y) (marked '(§1)').
- Addition and subtraction are componentwise.
- Multiplication: (x + y theta)(x' + y' theta) = xx' + (xy' + yx') theta + yy' theta^2. Substituting theta^2 = b theta - c [my step] gives (xx' - c yy') + (xy' + yx' + b yy') theta. In pair notation: (x, y)(x', y') = (xx' - cyy', xy' + yx' + byy').
- Division (headed §4a by accident of layout): multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate x + y(b - theta) = x + by - y theta. The conjugate root is b - theta, since the roots sum to b.
  - Denominator (the norm): (x + y theta)(x + by - y theta) = x(x + by) + c y^2. This uses theta(b - theta) = c [my step].
  - Numerator: ((x + by)x' + c yy') + {(x + by)y' - yx' - b yy'} theta.
  - The brace simplifies [my step] to xy' - yx'.
  - Result: (x', y')/(x, y) = ((xx' + bx'y + cyy')/(x^2 + bxy + cy^2), (xy' - yx')/(x^2 + bxy + cy^2)).
- Discriminant: det[[1, theta], [1, b - theta]] = b - 2 theta. Its square is [my step] b^2 - 4b theta + 4 theta^2 = b^2 - 4c = Delta, hence the label sqrt(Delta).
- Inverse matrix: Dedekind writes [[(b - theta)/(b - 2theta), -1/(b - 2theta)], [-theta/(b - 2theta), 1/(b - 2theta)]].
  - This is the inverse of the transpose [[1, 1], [theta, b - theta]].
  - Its first row is exactly the trace-dual (complementary) basis of {1, theta}, i.e. beta_i / f'(theta) with f'(theta) = 2 theta - b. Its second row is the conjugate of the first.
- He then clears the denominator b - 2theta:
  - (b - theta)(b - 2theta) = b^2 - 3b theta + 2theta^2 = b^2 - 3b theta + 2(b theta - c) = (b^2 - 2c) - b theta.
  - (-1)(b - 2theta) = -b + 2theta.
  - These compute (b - theta) sqrt(Delta) and -sqrt(Delta) in the basis {1, theta}, presumably toward the complementary module / different of Z[theta].
errors: Line 2: the product is written (xx' - cyy') + (xy' + yx' + byy') without the factor theta on the second term. This is a notational slip; the later pair version (xx' - cyy', xy' + yx' + byy') is correct.
The heading '§4a' sits next to the division formula only by layout. It belongs to the 'Intervalle' text, not to the computation.

The 'inverse' matrix is the inverse of the transposed discriminant matrix [[1, 1], [theta, b - theta]], not of [[1, theta], [1, b - theta]] as written. This is consistent if rows are read as the dual basis; it is not a real error.
All other computations check out: product, norm x^2 + bxy + cy^2, quotient, (b - 2theta)^2 = b^2 - 4c, and (b - theta)(b - 2theta) = b^2 - 2c - b theta.

results.what: Definition of an interval of rationals as a set containing every number between any two of its members; cut classes as special cases; characterization of a lower class as a downward-closed proper subset
results.modern_name: order-convex subset; lower set / Dedekind cut characterization
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (cuts, 1872); convex sets of an ordered set are folklore

results.what: Arithmetic in Q(theta), theta^2 = b theta - c: multiplication and division via the conjugate b - theta and the norm x^2 + bxy + cy^2
results.modern_name: arithmetic in a quadratic field; norm form

results.what: det[[1, theta], [1, b - theta]] = b - 2theta = sqrt(Delta), with Delta = b^2 - 4c
results.modern_name: discriminant of the basis {1, theta} as a squared Vandermonde determinant

results.what: Inverse of the basis-conjugate matrix, giving the dual basis (b - theta)/(b - 2theta), -1/(b - 2theta); these are then multiplied out by sqrt(Delta)
results.modern_name: trace-dual basis / complementary module (Euler's lemma), different

deep.surprise_reason: Both layers are routine and characteristically Dedekind. The interval notion elaborates his 1872 cut theory. The quadratic-field computation of the norm, discriminant and dual basis is elementary material from his own published algebraic number theory (complementary module, 1882).

transcription_corrections: Line 2 should read (x + y theta)(x' + y' theta) = (xx' - cyy') + (xy' + yx' + byy') in the manuscript, which itself omits theta; the intended reading has '... + (xy' + yx' + byy') theta'.
The numerator line reads ((x + by)x' + cyy') + {(x + by)y' - yx' - byy'} with theta implicit after the brace; the denominator is x(x + by) + cyy, as transcribed.
The pair product reads (x, y)(x', y') = (xx' - cyy', xy' + yx' + byy'); the final '+ byy'' is partly cut off at the margin in the image.
